subject: math
title: Grade 6 Multiplying and Dividing with Fractions
seo_title: Grade 6 Multiplying and Dividing with Fractions Worksheets: Fraction of a Number, Whole Number ÷ Fraction (Free, Answer Key, Ontario)
standard_text: Multiply and divide whole numbers by proper fractions, using appropriate tools and strategies
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 math worksheets on multiplying and dividing whole numbers by fractions for the Ontario curriculum: bar models, fractions of quantities, 3 ÷ 1/4 with pictures, 6 ÷ 2/3 and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key. Great EQAO practice.
key_big: × a fraction means “of”, so the answer gets smaller. ÷ a fraction asks how many pieces fit, so the answer gets bigger.
key_sub: 2/3 of 12 = 12 ÷ 3 × 2 = 8. 3 ÷ 1/4 = 12, because each whole has 4 fourths. 6 ÷ 2/3 = 6 × 3/2 = 9: flip only the fraction you divide by.
body_html:
The big idea

× a fraction means “of”. 23 × 12 means 23 of 12. ÷ a fraction asks “how many of these fit?” 3 ÷ 14 asks how many fourths fit in 3. Multiplying by a proper fraction gives a smaller answer. Dividing by one gives a bigger answer.

Fraction of a whole number

Divide by the denominator, then multiply by the numerator.

Example

What is 35 of 40 kg?

40 ÷ 5 = 8 kg in each part. 3 × 8 = 24.

Answer: 24 kg

Whole number × fraction

Multiply the whole number by the numerator and keep the denominator. Then change it to a mixed number.

Example

7 × 23 = ?

7 × 2 = 14, so the answer is 143. 14 ÷ 3 = 4 remainder 2.

Answer: 4 23

Whole number ÷ unit fraction

Count the pieces. Each whole has as many pieces as the denominator.

Example

5 ÷ 13 = ?

Each whole has 3 thirds. 5 × 3 = 15.

Answer: 15

Whole number ÷ proper fraction

Cut the wholes into pieces, then put the pieces into groups. Or use the rule: keep the whole number, flip only the fraction you divide by, and multiply.

Example

6 ÷ 23 = ?

Flip 23 to 32. 6 × 32 = 182 = 9. Check: 9 × 23 = 183 = 6.

Answer: 9

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
3 ÷ 14 = 34 (thinking dividing always makes a number smaller)Dividing by a fraction less than 1 gives a bigger answer: there are 12 fourths in 3.
4 ÷ 25 = 14 × 25 = 110 (flipping the wrong number)Keep 4, flip only 25: 4 × 52 = 10.
5 × 34 = 1520 (multiplying the denominator too)Only multiply the numerator: 154 = 3 34.
5 ÷ 23 = 7 13 (leftover written as part of a whole)15 thirds make 7 groups of 2 and 1 third left. 1 third is 12 of a group: 7 12.

faq.q: How do you multiply a whole number by a fraction in Grade 6?
faq.a: Multiply the whole number by the numerator and keep the denominator, then simplify. For example, 5 × 3/4 = 15/4 = 3 3/4, and 2/3 of 12 = 12 ÷ 3 × 2 = 8.

faq.q: How do you divide a whole number by a fraction?
faq.a: Keep the whole number, flip only the fraction you divide by, and multiply. For example, 6 ÷ 2/3 = 6 × 3/2 = 9, and 3 ÷ 1/4 = 3 × 4 = 12.

faq.q: Why is the answer bigger when you divide by a fraction?
faq.a: Dividing asks how many pieces fit. A piece smaller than 1 fits more times than 1 does, so 3 ÷ 1/4 = 12 is bigger than 3.

faq.q: Is multiplying and dividing with fractions on the Grade 6 EQAO math test?
faq.a: The Grade 6 EQAO math assessment is based on the Ontario curriculum, and multiplying and dividing whole numbers by fractions is part of the Grade 6 Number strand. Practising fraction word problems like these is good preparation.

items.q: The whole bar is 12. The shaded part shows 23 × 12. What is 23 × 12?
items.e: 23 × 12 means 23 of 12. Divide by the denominator: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 2 × 4 = 8. So 23 of 12 = 8.

items.q: The whole bar is 20. The shaded part shows 34 × 20. What is 34 × 20?
items.e: 34 × 20 means 34 of 20. Divide by the denominator: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 5 = 15. So 34 of 20 = 15.

items.q: The whole bar is 30. The shaded part shows 25 × 30. What is 25 × 30?
items.e: 25 × 30 means 25 of 30. Divide by the denominator: 30 ÷ 5 = 6 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 2 × 6 = 12. So 25 of 30 = 12.

items.q: The whole bar is 18. The shaded part shows 56 × 18. What is 56 × 18?
items.e: 56 × 18 means 56 of 18. Divide by the denominator: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 5 × 3 = 15. So 56 of 18 = 15.

items.q: What is 34 of 24 kg?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 kg in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 6 = 18 kg. So 34 of 24 kg = 18 kg.

items.q: What is 25 of 35 m?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 35 ÷ 5 = 7 m in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 2 × 7 = 14 m. So 25 of 35 m = 14 m.

items.q: What is 34 of $20?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: $20 ÷ 4 = $5 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × $5 = $15. So 34 of $20 = $15.

items.q: What is 23 of 60 min?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 60 ÷ 3 = 20 min in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 2 × 20 = 40 min. So 23 of 60 min = 40 min.

items.q: What is 58 of 64 cm?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 64 ÷ 8 = 8 cm in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 5 × 8 = 40 cm. So 58 of 64 cm = 40 cm.

items.q: What is 710 of 50 L?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 50 ÷ 10 = 5 L in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 7 × 5 = 35 L. So 710 of 50 L = 35 L.

items.q: What is 35 of 2500 m?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 2500 ÷ 5 = 500 m in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 500 = 1500 m. So 35 of 2500 m = 1500 m.

items.q: What is 56 of 42 km?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 42 ÷ 6 = 7 km in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 5 × 7 = 35 km. So 56 of 42 km = 35 km.

items.q: What is 49 of 54 mL?

items.q: What is 23 of 4500 g?

items.q: What is 512 of 60 min?

items.q: What is 37 of 140 kg?

items.q: 25 of a number is 14. What is the number?
items.e: 2 parts are 14, so 1 part is 14 ÷ 2 = 7. The whole has 5 parts: 7 × 5 = 35. Check: 25 of 35 = 35 ÷ 5 × 2 = 14.

items.q: 34 of a number is 27. What is the number?
items.e: 3 parts are 27, so 1 part is 27 ÷ 3 = 9. The whole has 4 parts: 9 × 4 = 36. Check: 34 of 36 = 36 ÷ 4 × 3 = 27.

items.q: 56 of a number is 40. What is the number?
items.e: 5 parts are 40, so 1 part is 40 ÷ 5 = 8. The whole has 6 parts: 8 × 6 = 48. Check: 56 of 48 = 48 ÷ 6 × 5 = 40.

items.q: Which is greater: 34 of 20 or 23 of 24?
items.e: 34 of 20: 20 ÷ 4 = 5, 5 × 3 = 15. 23 of 24: 24 ÷ 3 = 8, 8 × 2 = 16. 16 is greater than 15, so 23 of 24 is greater.

items.q: 3? of 40 = 15. What is the missing denominator?
items.e: 15 is 3 parts, so 1 part is 15 ÷ 3 = 5. 40 ÷ 5 = 8, so 40 is split into 8 equal parts: 38 of 40 = 15. The missing denominator is 8.

items.q: ?5 of 30 = 18. What is the missing numerator?
items.e: 30 ÷ 5 = 6, so each fifth of 30 is 6. 18 ÷ 6 = 3 parts, so 35 of 30 = 18. The missing numerator is 3.

items.q: Which is the same as 6 ÷ 13?
c: 16 × 13

items.q: Without calculating, which is true about 4 ÷ 12?
items.e: There are 2 halves in every whole, so there are more halves than wholes. 4 ÷ 12 = 8, which is greater than 4. Dividing by a fraction less than 1 gives a bigger answer.

items.q: Without calculating, which answer is greater than 12?
items.e: Multiplying by 34 or taking 34 of 12 gives less than 12, and 12 ÷ 4 = 3. Dividing by a fraction less than 1 gives more: 12 ÷ 34 = 16.

items.q: Maya says 6 ÷ 23 = 4. What did she do?
c: She multiplied by 23 instead of dividing.
She flipped 6 instead of 23.
items.e: 6 × 23 = 4, so Maya multiplied. Dividing by a fraction less than 1 must give more than 6: 6 ÷ 23 = 6 × 32 = 182 = 9.

items.q: Mei says 4 ÷ 25 = 110. What did she do?
c: She multiplied by 25 instead of dividing.
She flipped 4 instead of 25.
items.e: 14 × 25 = 220 = 110, so Mei flipped the wrong number. Keep 4 and flip only the divisor: 4 × 52 = 202 = 10.

items.q: A bag holds 3 cups of trail mix. One serving is 14 cup. How many servings are in the bag?
items.e: How many 14 cups are in 3 cups? 3 ÷ 14. Each whole has 4 fourths. 3 wholes have 3 × 4 = 12 fourths, so 3 ÷ 14 = 12 servings. Check: 12 × 14 = 124 = 3.

items.q: There are 24 students in a Grade 6 class. 23 of them go on the field trip to the science centre. How many students go?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 students in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 2 × 8 = 16 students. So 23 of 24 students = 16 students.

items.q: A sugar shack has 6 L of maple syrup. It fills bottles that each hold 34 L. How many bottles can it fill?
items.e: 6 ÷ 34. Each whole has 4 fourths, so 6 wholes have 6 × 4 = 24 fourths. Each group is 34 = 3 fourths. 24 ÷ 3 = 8 groups. Or flip only the divisor: 6 × 43 = 243. So 6 ÷ 34 = 8 bottles. Check: 8 × 34 = 6.

items.q: Liam practises skating for 34 h a day, 6 days a week. How many hours is that each week?
items.e: 6 × 34: Multiply the whole number by the numerator and keep the denominator: 6 × 3 = 18, so the answer is 184. Simplify: 184 = 92. 9 ÷ 2 = 4 remainder 1, so it is 4 12 h.

items.q: The Terry Fox Run route at Priya’s school is 5 km. She has run 35 of the route. How far has she run?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 5 ÷ 5 = 1 km in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 1 = 3 km. So 35 of 5 km = 3 km.

items.q: A toque costs $24. In a sale, Arjun pays 34 of the price. How much does he pay?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: $24 ÷ 4 = $6 in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × $6 = $18. So 34 of $24 = $18.

items.q: A 6 m roll of ribbon is cut into pieces that are each 23 m long. How many pieces are there?
items.e: 6 ÷ 23. Each whole has 3 thirds, so 6 wholes have 6 × 3 = 18 thirds. Each group is 23 = 2 thirds. 18 ÷ 2 = 9 groups. Or flip only the divisor: 6 × 32 = 182. So 6 ÷ 23 = 9 pieces. Check: 9 × 23 = 6.

items.q: A canoe trip is 12 km long. The group paddles 13 of the route before lunch. How far do they paddle before lunch?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 km in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 1 × 4 = 4 km. So 13 of 12 km = 4 km.

items.q: Owen orders 3 pizzas for a team party. Each player gets 38 of a pizza. How many players can he feed?
items.e: 3 ÷ 38. Each whole has 8 eighths, so 3 wholes have 3 × 8 = 24 eighths. Each group is 38 = 3 eighths. 24 ÷ 3 = 8 groups. Or flip only the divisor: 3 × 83 = 243. So 3 ÷ 38 = 8 players. Check: 8 × 38 = 3.

items.q: One batch of maple cookies needs 23 cup of flour. How much flour do 4 batches need?
items.e: 4 × 23: Multiply the whole number by the numerator and keep the denominator: 4 × 2 = 8, so the answer is 83. 8 ÷ 3 = 2 remainder 2, so it is 2 23 cups.

items.q: Mateo reads for 14 h every night. How many nights does it take him to read for 5 h?
items.e: 5 ÷ 14. Each whole has 4 fourths. 5 wholes have 5 × 4 = 20 fourths, so 5 ÷ 14 = 20 nights. Check: 20 × 14 = 204 = 5.

items.q: The Grade 6 bake sale has 45 muffins. 35 of them are sold by recess. How many muffins are sold by recess?
items.e: Divide by the denominator: 45 ÷ 5 = 9 muffins in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 3 × 9 = 27 muffins. So 35 of 45 muffins = 27 muffins.

items.q: At the cottage, Ava cuts a 10 m board into shelves that are each 56 m long. How many shelves does she get?
items.e: 10 ÷ 56. Each whole has 6 sixths, so 10 wholes have 10 × 6 = 60 sixths. Each group is 56 = 5 sixths. 60 ÷ 5 = 12 groups. Or flip only the divisor: 10 × 65 = 605. So 10 ÷ 56 = 12 shelves. Check: 12 × 56 = 10.

items.q: Lucas drinks 34 L of water at school each day. How much does he drink in 5 school days?
items.e: 5 × 34: Multiply the whole number by the numerator and keep the denominator: 5 × 3 = 15, so the answer is 154. 15 ÷ 4 = 3 remainder 3, so it is 3 34 L.

items.q: A hockey game has three 20-minute periods. Benjamin is on the ice for 25 of the game time. How many minutes is that?
items.e: The game is 3 × 20 = 60 min. Divide by the denominator: 60 ÷ 5 = 12 min in each part. Multiply by the numerator: 2 × 12 = 24 min. So 25 of 60 min = 24 min.

items.q: Chloe has saved $30. That is 35 of the cost of new skates. How much do the skates cost?
items.e: 3 parts are $30, so 1 part is $30 ÷ 3 = $10. The whole cost has 5 parts: 5 × $10 = $50. Check: 35 of $50 = $50 ÷ 5 × 3 = $30.

items.q: A 4 L jug of apple cider is poured into cups that each hold 15 L. Which expression gives the number of cups?
items.e: The question asks how many 15 L cups fit in 4 L, so divide 4 by 15: 4 ÷ 15 = 4 × 5 = 20 cups.

items.q: One batch of pancakes needs 34 cup of milk. Hana has 5 cups of milk. How many full batches can she make?
items.e: 5 ÷ 34. Each whole has 4 fourths, so 5 wholes have 5 × 4 = 20 fourths. Each group is 34 = 3 fourths. 20 ÷ 3 = 6 remainder 2. The 2 fourths left over are 23 of a group. Or flip only the divisor: 5 × 43 = 203. So 5 ÷ 34 = 6 23. Check: 6 23 × 34 = 5. Only whole batches count, so she can make 6 batches.

items.q: Sofia walks 34 km to school and 34 km home every day. How far does she walk in 5 school days?
items.e: Each day: 2 × 34 = 64 km. In 5 days: 10 × 34. Multiply the whole number by the numerator and keep the denominator: 10 × 3 = 30, so the answer is 304. Simplify: 304 = 152. 15 ÷ 2 = 7 remainder 1, so it is 7 12 km.

items.q: On a snow day, Noah fills buckets of snow to build a fort. Each bucket holds 25 of a wheelbarrow load. How many buckets fill 4 wheelbarrows?
items.e: 4 ÷ 25. Each whole has 5 fifths, so 4 wholes have 4 × 5 = 20 fifths. Each group is 25 = 2 fifths. 20 ÷ 2 = 10 groups. Or flip only the divisor: 4 × 52 = 202. So 4 ÷ 25 = 10 buckets. Check: 10 × 25 = 4.
